decisive_items: Gram stain from all three sets showed gram-negative bacilli
response.rationale: Gram-negative bacteremia is confirmed by gram-negative bacilli in all blood cultures, and fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and elevated CRP define the septic response. R4 is the most specific fully supported label; R3 captures bacteremia but not sepsis, R2 is too broad, R1 is unsupported by the culture timing and normal catheter site, and R5 lacks species evidence for Pseudomonas.

rejected.why: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is not specified; gram-negative bacilli on Gram stain do not identify the species.
Sepsis is supported but omits the confirmed gram-negative bacillary bacteremia.
Catheter source is not supported because the peripheral culture became positive earlier than the catheter cultures and the catheter site had no local signs.
Gram-negative bacteremia is supported but less complete because it omits the sepsis syndrome evident from fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and elevated CRP.
